result.summary: The proposed sweep still permits deletion of quarantined originals on case-insensitive filesystems.

findings.title: Protect case variants of the quarantine directory before recursive deletion
findings.body: X1 step 2 recursively deletes every child not named exactly `quarantine`. On a case-insensitive filesystem, an existing `Quarantine` directory is also the destination of quarantinePreserve's lowercase path, but enumeration retains its capitalized name. If that directory is empty at the gate and a dream completes a preserve before the sweep, step 2 recursively destroys the new original before the protected rmdir sequence runs. Case-insensitive path identity was verified on this workspace; an in-memory execution of the specified sequence reproduced the deletion. The top-down symlink checks do not cover this case.
findings.recommendation: Exclude all ASCII case variants of `quarantine` from recursive removal, conservatively preserving ambiguous entries. Add a regression with an empty capitalized shelf at inventory time and a completed preserve between inventory and deletion; assert the original bytes survive.

next_steps: Revise X1 and its mirrored contracts, and add the case-insensitive interleaving regression before dispatch.
